rules.statement: In test scripts, don't copy the same helper function into several stand-in or fake scripts; put it in one shared helper file that each stand-in dot-sources (and that the fixture copies beside every stand-in it places).
rules.why: A later fix, such as to locking, would otherwise have to be repeated in every copy, and the copies drift apart.
rules.check: Look for a function body that is identical or nearly identical in two or more test stand-in scripts instead of being dot-sourced from one shared file.

rules.statement: In test code, when several concurrent processes or runspaces append to a shared log file under a named mutex, catch AbandonedMutexException around WaitOne and continue, and derive the mutex name from a hash (such as SHA-256) of the log file's full path so every writer to the same file shares one mutex.
rules.why: If a holder dies while it holds the mutex, a bare WaitOne throws on the next call and writers handle the same case differently. A name taken from the path makes sure writers to one file use the same lock.
rules.check: Look for WaitOne calls on a named mutex without an AbandonedMutexException handler, and for mutex names that are hard-coded or not derived from the full path of the file they guard.
